title: rwb-access booking confirmation: the authorise request and answer shapes, the contract entry of the authorise path and the rwb-access login are not specified
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14 and 41; TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T-A.1 and T6.1; FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A2.4; Legacy RWB-E2-007 sections 10, 12 and 13
section: Section 3 Preconditions; section 10 Authority; section 12.1, 12.8 and 12.9 Contract; section 13 Solution plan; section 15 Screens and states
description: Three values this slice needs are absent or unresolved. (1) Architecture v5 slides 14 and 41 name POST /authorise the first API path of rwb-access (with GET /me/permissions, GET /doa-limits and /masking-policies), but the TSD P4 appendix T-A endpoint inventory has no authorise path and no request or answer schema, so the fields the caller sends (identity, capability area, right, case and treatment reference, field IDs, the case attributes for the scope test) and the fields the answer returns (decision code, matrix version, masking answer, scope result, entry reference) are a read, not a source value. (2) The per-service database login for rwb-access is named nowhere; the story uses 'the rwb-access login (DP-02)' as a placeholder. (3) The gateway-bff composite route behind SCR-14 Treatment record and SCR-01 My work has no field list, hop list or masking detail (DP-19).
evidence: Arch v5 slide 41 gives rwb-access the first API path /authorise and slide 14 lists it as an IN operation with 'cached'; TSD P4 T-A.1 lists API-P4-004 to API-P4-021 and none of them is the authorise path; TSD P4 T3.1 defines no authorise object; Legacy RWB-E2-007 section 10 names roles and rights but no request shape, and section 13 names no login and no screen route.
area: rwb-access contract, configuration and screen composition
proposed: Add the authorise path with its request and answer schema to the API specification and TSD P4 appendix T-A, publish it with RWB-P4-E1037-CON and stub it in that contract fake, fix the rwb-access login in the platform DB story, and publish the composite route with gateway-bff (DP-19).

title: rwb-access booking confirmation: the TSD RBAC matrix has no Case record column, so the CASE_RECORD R and U letters the booking tasks need are not tabulated
source: TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T6.1 and T3.2; FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A2.4 and A2.7; Legacy RWB-E2-007 sections 4 steps 7 and 8 and 10
section: Section 3 Preconditions; section 8 Business rules BR5; section 13 Configuration and reference data
description: The legacy flow opens WITH_OPS_BOOKING, WITH_OPS_SETTLEMENT and UNMATCHED_EXCEPTION for RW-RESTRUCT and RW-CREDITAD and closes them on the case record, and FSD A2.4 defines the matrix over the 14 capability areas of LOV-CAPABILITY, which includes CASE_RECORD and TREATMENT_AND_OFFER. The TSD P4 RBAC matrix tabulates only three columns - Rules and parameters, Reference data and Platform administration - and gives no letter for any role in Case record or Treatment and offer, so the two letters this capability needs (CASE_RECORD R and U, TREATMENT_AND_OFFER R for RW-RESTRUCT and RW-CREDITAD) are carried by the policy pack read in this story and not by a source table.
evidence: TSD P4 T6.1 rows run 'RW-CASEOWN Case owner | R | R | -' to 'SY-AGENT Agent platform | R | R | -' with the three column headers only; LOV-CAPABILITY in T3.2 lists CASE_RECORD and TREATMENT_AND_OFFER; FSD P4 A2.4 AC-ALT-P4-004-02 refuses RW-CASEOWN the QUEUE_AND_ALLOCATION U right, which shows the matrix is per area, while no Case record letter appears anywhere in T6.1.
proposed: Extend the T6.1 matrix with the Case record and Treatment and offer columns, publish the full 14-area matrix version as data with RWB-P4-AD002-APP, and confirm the two roles' letters with the matrix owner before the pack goes in force.

title: rwb-access booking confirmation: the lifetime of a cached authorise decision is not specified
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 14 ('Access: authorise (cached)') and slide 20; DP-11; TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T6.2; Legacy RWB-E2-007 section 12
section: Section 3 Preconditions; section 7 AC7; section 12.1 Contract; section 13 Configuration and reference data
description: Architecture v5 names the authorise decision 'cached' and DP-11 fixes one hop and a 2 s timeout, but no source gives the lifetime of a cached decision, the size of the cache, or whether a refused decision is cached with an allowed one. This story serves the decision from a cache keyed on identity, area, right, case reference, field list and matrix version, and drops it when the pack version changes; the lifetime itself is read as a parameter and its value is not in the sources.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 14 OUT line of rwb-access reads 'REST Access: authorise (cached)' with no lifetime; TSD P4 T6.2 describes the access check but names no cache; the FSD A2.4 criteria test a grant and a refusal but no expiry; no parameter row for the cache appears in the TSD or the FSD.
proposed: Fix the lifetime as a parameter of the parameters contract (DP-06) with its value agreed at the wave 2 design review, and test the version-keyed drop rather than the clock so the behaviour holds whatever value is agreed.

title: POST /authorise request and response shape is not specified for the payment-matching reads
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 14; TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T6.2; FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A2.7
section: Slide 14 rwb-access IN (POST /authorise (role, scope, DoA)); TSD P4 T6.2; FSD P4 A2.7.4
description: The architecture names the authorise call and three field groups only. The payment-matching read needs the capability area, the right, the resolved scope, the resource, the filter and the row count of the answer, and the matrix version applied, and none of these has a named field in the request or the answer. The three answers of this slice (allow, refuse by right, refuse by scope) also have no named representation.
evidence: Slide 14 and the slide notes give only 'POST /authorise (role, scope, DoA)'; TSD P4 T6.2 says each endpoint declares its capability area and right without an envelope; FSD A2.7 AC-P4-007-01 and AC-ALT-P4-007-02 require the case ID or the filter and row count in the entry.
proposed: Extend the RWB-P4-E1037-CON envelope with area, right, scope, resource, filter, rowCount and matrixVersion, and fix the three answer codes, at the contract review for wave 2.

title: Permission letters for WRITE_OFF_AND_POSTING and TREATMENT_AND_OFFER and the scope of the Credit Administration role are absent from the RBAC matrix
source: TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T6.1 and T3.2; FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A2.4; legacy RWB-E2-008 section 10
section: TSD P4 T6.1 RBAC matrix; T3.2 LOV-CAPABILITY and LOV-SCOPE
description: T6.1 holds three columns only (Rules and parameters, Reference data, Platform administration), while LOV-CAPABILITY defines 14 capability areas. The letters this capability depends on (Write-off and posting R for RW-CREDITAD and SY-AGENT, Treatment and offer R for RW-CASEOWN, none for RW-CASEOWN on Write-off and posting, R with scope ALL for RW-AUDIT) and the default scope value of RW-CREDITAD are therefore not in the matrix and cannot be transcribed into the policy pack from the technical specification.
evidence: TSD P4 T6.1 rows give RW-CREDITAD 'R | R | -' and RW-CASEOWN 'R | R | -' with no Write-off and posting or Treatment and offer column; legacy RWB-E2-008 section 10 gives the same roles different rights (CRUA on SCR-28, R on SCR-14).
proposed: Publish the letters of all 14 capability areas per role, with the default scope of each role, as a new TSD P4 T6.1 version, and load them through RWB-P4-AD002-APP.

title: The field that carries the filter and the row count in an AC-READ or AC-DENY entry is not specified
source: FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A2.7 AC-ALT-P4-007-02; TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T6.3; Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8 DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018
section: FSD P4 A2.7.4.2; TSD P4 T6.3; DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018
description: The functional specification requires an export or list read to record the filter, the row count and no case ID, and the decision-record entry is the only access log this run allows. The decision-record field set of DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 names no filter, no row count and no capability area, so the place these values take in the entry is unspecified.
evidence: FSD P4 AC-ALT-P4-007-02 requires decision code 'AC-EXPT', the filter, row count 37 and no case ID; TSD P4 T6.3 lists only rule linkage for the decision log; the LDM entry fields carry no filter or count.
proposed: Carry the filter and the row count in the actions list of the decision-record entry, and add the capability area and the right to the same list in the next LDM version.

title: GET /doa-limits is named in Architecture v5 and API v3 but absent from API Specification v4
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json
section: Slide 14 P4 rwb-access IN: REST POST /authorise (role, scope, DoA); GET /me/permissions; GET /doa-limits /masking-policies; ownership.json delegation_limit basis (API Specification v3 GET /doa-limits x_module P4)
description: Architecture v5 gives rwb-access the DoA limits read as an inbound REST operation and the ownership map cites API Specification v3 for GET /doa-limits with x_module P4, but the operation has no row in API Specification v4. The story needs the operation on the published base /api/recovery/access/v1 to answer the approval router.
evidence: Architecture v5 slides 14 and 41 note for rwb-access: IN REST ... GET /doa-limits; ownership.json delegation_limit basis cites API Specification v3 GET /doa-limits x_module P4; API Specification v4 carries no /doa-limits row and TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A has no such endpoint
proposed: Add GET /api/recovery/access/v1/doa-limits to the API Specification baseline as a P4 operation with the query and response fields this story uses, and correct the v4 omission in favour of Architecture v5 under R-PREC.

title: The DoA lookup and authority-decision request and response shape is not specified
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P4 Access and administration v3.md; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md
section: FSD P4 v3 A2.6 (the lookup returns the level, the row ID and the version); Architecture v5 slide 14 (GET /doa-limits, no schema)
description: FSD A2.6 says only that the lookup answers the level, the row ID and the version; it names no query parameters, no field names and no outcome values. The story needs the request to carry the decision, the regulation item, the product group, the amounts, the related-party flag and the routing date, and the response to carry level, row, version, holder, substitute and outcome; the DoA part of POST /authorise has the same gap.
evidence: FSD P4 v3 AC-ALT-P4-006-01 says the lookup returns level L6, the row ID of item 2.1.1 at L6 and version DOA-2026.11; no request or response schema in FSD P4 v3, in TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A or in Architecture v5
proposed: Freeze the request and response field set written in this story at the contract review, with the five outcome values COVERED, NO_HOLDER, NOT_COVERED, NO_AMOUNT_LIMIT and RELATED_PARTY and the requiredLevel carried on a refused authority decision.

title: The scope of the rwb-decision service identity inside rwb-access is not specified
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md
section: TSD P4 v3 T6.1 RBAC matrix and T6.2 authentication and authorization; Architecture v5 slides 14 and 41 (P7 IN: REST Access: DoA limits)
description: Architecture v5 has rwb-decision read the DoA limits and TSD P4 T6.1 lists the RW- roles and a few service identities, but no row gives the rwb-decision service identity a right in any capability area. The story assumes Approval check R for that identity and cannot say what else it may read or do.
evidence: TSD P4 v3 T6.1 has service rows for SY-CASEWF, SY-RULES, SY-DATALOAD, SY-OCR and SY-AGENT only; Architecture v5 slide 41 P7 IN names REST Access: DoA limits without a right; no source names the rwb-decision identity
proposed: Add the rwb-decision service identity to the permission data with Approval check R and no other Recovery right, and confirm it with the security administrator before the authorise contract is frozen.

title: The masked rendering of the addressee postal address is not specified
source: Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md; Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P4 Access and administration v3.md; Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8
section: TSD P4 v3 T3.1 masking_rule (DF-REF-198 to DF-REF-204); FSD P4 v3 A2.5; LDM v8 DF-PTY-016
description: The masking_rule table carries role_code, field_id, unmasked, masking_version and validity, and no column or rule fixes how a masked value is rendered. FSD A2.5 gives a rendering for an identity number and a date of birth only. The addressee postal address DF-PTY-016 (contact_point.value_token over v_ace_contact.contact_value), which the D7.1 notice shows on SCR-11 and SCR-18, therefore has no specified mask format, so the story names the field and the mask version and asserts only that the value is absent.
evidence: TSD P4 v3 T3.1 masking_rule: DF-REF-198 id, 199 role_code, 200 field_id, 201 unmasked, 202 masking_version, 203 valid_from, 204 valid_to; FSD P4 v3 AC-ALT-P4-004-01 gives XXXXXXXX1234 and XXXXXX5678 for other fields; FSD P4 v3 AC-EXC-P4-004-05 gives XXXX-XX-XX for v_ace_customer.date_of_birth; no source gives a postal address format
owner_role: Compliance and PDPA officer with the P4 solution architect
proposed: Let the platform masking library own one rendering per field type, record it as data beside the masking row, and add the postal address rendering to the MASK-SIT-01 pack before the first SIT run of the approval screen

title: The request and response shape of the authorise operation is not specified
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md; Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md
section: Arch v5 slide 14 and slide 41 (rwb-access IN: REST POST /authorise (role, scope, DoA); GET /me/permissions; /masking-policies); TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A
description: Architecture v5 names the authorise operation and its purpose and nothing more; TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A lists API-P4-004 to API-P4-021 and does not define the authorise path at all, and it names GET /me/session (API-P4-012) where Arch v5 names GET /me/permissions. No source gives the fields of the authorise request or response, the field-marker shape, or whether the routed role or the holder travels in the request.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 14: 'IN: REST POST /authorise (role, scope, DoA); GET /me/permissions; GET /doa-limits /masking-policies'; TSD P4 v3 T-A.1 endpoint inventory holds no /authorise row; TSD P4 v3 API-P4-012 GET /me/session purpose 'Read the caller's resolved session'
area: Access and authority (P4 rwb-access); API contract
proposed: Publish the authorise, me-permissions and masking-policies shapes in the P4 contract story RWB-P4-E1037-CON before the screen story is built, and state in it whether the routed role or the holder is a request field

title: The masking version in force in SIT is not recorded anywhere
source: Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P4 Access and administration v3.md; Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md
section: FSD P4 v3 A2.5 AC-EXC-P4-004-05 (no masking rule in MASK-SIT-01); TSD P4 v3 T3.1 masking_rule.masking_version (DF-REF-202)
description: The masking version appears only inside two FSD acceptance criteria that name MASK-SIT-01 for a SIT example; no environment, pack or load record states which masking version is in force in SIT, who approves it, or its valid-from date. The story therefore assumes MASK-SIT-01 for its SIT tests and reads the version from the rows at run time rather than configuring it.
evidence: FSD P4 v3 AC-EXC-P4-004-05: 'no masking rule in MASK-SIT-01 covers v_ace_customer.date_of_birth for any role'; TSD P4 v3 DF-REF-202 masking_version varchar(20) with no seeded value; no load record or environment table in either module
area: Access and authority (P4 rwb-access); masking policy pack
owner_role: Compliance and PDPA officer with the P4 build squad
proposed: Record the masking version in force per environment in the policy pack load record, with its approver and valid-from date, and assert it in the SIT entry check

title: The object attributes an authorise request carries are not specified
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 14 (P4 IN: POST /authorise role, scope, DoA); FSD P4 v3 A2.4, A2.14; TSD P4 v3 T-A.2; legacy RWB-E2-015 section 12
section: Story s1, s3, s4 step 2, s8 BR2 and BR3, s11
description: The access decision needs the case, its team, its owner and, for the escalation grant, the role a SERVICE_LEVEL timer is escalated to and the time it was escalated. No source names the attribute set of an authorise request, its field names or which attributes are mandatory, so the service cannot be built against a fixed request shape.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 14 gives only 'POST /authorise (role, scope, DoA)'; FSD P4 A2.4 and A2.14 give the matrix and the scope rule but no request payload; TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A holds no authorise endpoint of its own; legacy RWB-E2-015 section 12 reads the facts from GET /cases/{caseId} and GET /cases/{caseId}/timers, which no longer cross the service boundary.
proposed: Fix the authorise request in RWB-P4-E1037-CON with caseId, teamCode, ownerUserRef, escalatedToRole and escalatedAt, and version it as v1 with BACKWARD compatibility so a case service adds an attribute without breaking the access service.

title: Precedence between a role's default scope and an escalation grant is not specified
source: FSD P4 v3 A2.14; TSD P4 v3 T3.2 LOV-SCOPE; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-UNI-30; legacy RWB-E2-015 AC4
section: Story s4 step 6, s8 BR3, s9
description: A case may be admitted by the caller's own scope and by an escalation to a role the caller holds at the same time. No source says which scope the answer names then, whether the reason is still ESCALATED_TO_ROLE, or whether an escalation can widen a read that the role's own scope already narrows to OWN.
evidence: FSD P4 A2.14 gives the scope rule only; R-UNI-30 says the breach is raised to the named escalation point and the case does not move; legacy RWB-E2-015 AC4 shows the escalation line but no scope answer, because that scope was enforced inside one module.
proposed: Rule that the wider of the two scopes is named, that the reason ESCALATED_TO_ROLE is carried while the escalation is open, and that the grant never exceeds Case record R on that one case.

title: The masking version in force for SIT and the answer when two versions overlap are not specified
source: FSD P4 v3 A2.5, AC-EXC-P4-004-05; TSD P4 v3 T3.1 masking_rule; legacy RWB-E2-015 section 13
section: Story s3, s4 step 7, s5, s13 configuration, s16
description: The source names MASK-SIT-01 only inside an exception path and never says which masking version is in force for the SIT environment of wave 2, nor how the answer behaves on a day when two masking versions have the same valid_from or overlap. A wrong default would show a personal field clear.
evidence: FSD P4 AC-EXC-P4-004-05 says 'no masking rule in MASK-SIT-01 covers v_ace_customer.date_of_birth'; TSD P4 T3.1 gives masking_rule.masking_version and valid_from without an in-force rule; the legacy story carries no masking version at all.
proposed: Record MASK-SIT-01 as the SIT version in the policy pack, and rule that the version with the latest valid_from on or before the business date is used, the answer naming the version it used.
